entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5782"/><title type="x-s2">PSALM 31</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Ps.31.1-Ps.31.24">Psa 31:1-24</reference>. The prayer of a believer in time of deep distress. In the first part, cries for help are mingled with expressions of confidence. Then the detail of griefs engrosses his attention, till, in the assurance of strong but submissive faith, he rises to the language of unmingled joyful trust and exhorts others to like love and confidence towards God.</title> <div sID="gen8800" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5782"/>1. Expresses the general tone of feeling of the Psalm. <div eID="gen8800" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5783"/><div sID="gen8801" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5783"/>2-4. He seeks help in God's righteous government (<reference osisRef="Ps.5.8">Psa 5:8</reference>), and begs for an attentive hearing, and speedy and effectual aid. With no other help and no claim of merit, he relies solely on God's regard to His own perfections for a safe guidance and release from the snares of his enemies. On the terms "rock," &c., (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.17.2">Psa 17:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.18.2">18:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.18.50">50</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.20.6">20:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.23.3">23:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.25.21">25:21</reference>). <div eID="gen8801" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 2-4. He seeks help in God's righteous government ( Psa 5:8 ), and begs for an attentive hearing, and speedy and effectual aid. With no other help and no claim of merit, he relies solely on God's regard to His own perfections for a safe guidance and release from the snares of his enemies. On the terms "rock," &c., (compare Psa 17:2 ; 18:2 , 50 ; 20:6 ; 23:3 ; 25:21 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5784"/><div sID="gen8802" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5784"/><hi type="bold">5-6. commit my spirit--</hi>my life, or myself. Our Saviour used the words on the Cross [Lu 23:46], not as prophetical, but, as many pious men have done, as expressive of His unshaken confidence in God. The Psalmist rests on God's faithfulness to His promises to His people, and hence avows himself one of them, detesting all who revere objects of idolatry (compare <reference osisRef="Deut.32.21">De 32:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor.8.4">1Co 8:4</reference>). <div eID="gen8802" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 5-6. commit my spirit-- my life, or myself. Our Saviour used the words on the Cross [Lu 23:46], not as prophetical, but, as many pious men have done, as expressive of His unshaken confidence in God. The Psalmist rests on God's faithfulness to His promises to His people, and hence avows himself one of them, detesting all who revere objects of idolatry (compare De 32:21 ; 1Co 8:4 ).
